reelection.rule: Rule: next even-year November for this House term. legislators-current.yaml ends the current term on 2027-01-03. The even-year November before that January 3 end is November 2026. The file has no election day, so no day of the month is shown.

vote_frequency.label: In this cached set only (the latest 40 House roll calls, not a lifetime record): 40 of 40. Yea or Aye: 35. Nay or No: 5. Not Voting: 0. Of 40 Yea or Nay votes where the Republican majority could be computed, 36 (90%) matched that majority (majority = the side most of that party's members voting Yea or Nay took; on average 210 members of that party voted Yea or Nay per roll call).

said_voted.caption: Posts are shown as written. A post is matched to a vote only when it names the bill number or the bill's official title. A post can mention a bill for many reasons.
said_voted.topic_caption: Recent posts grouped by simple keyword rules that are identical for every member (published at /x_topic_rules.json). A post listed under a topic is not claimed to be about any specific vote; a post can appear under more than one topic.

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Pass, as Amended — Housing for the 21st Century Act (H R 6644)
roll_calls.plain_language: This bill establishes and modifies various federal housing programs. This vote was under suspension of the rules, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea supports passing it as amended; a Nay opposes it.

roll_calls.question: On Motion to Suspend the Rules and Concur in Senate Adt to House Adt to Senate Adt — Housing for the 21st Century Act (H R 6644)
roll_calls.plain_language: The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act establishes and modifies various federal housing programs. This vote, under suspension of the rules, was on accepting the Senate's latest changes to the bill after the chambers traded versions, so a two-thirds vote was required. A Yea accepts the Senate's version; a Nay opposes it.

conflicts.caption: These are overlaps in public records, not evidence of a deal. Lobbying can be for or against a bill, and donors' employers didn't necessarily give money.
